newsitem.title: USA: Southern Air bullish on Brazil, cargo charters.
newsitem.headline: Southern Air bullish on Brazil, cargo charters.

text.p: Southern Air Transport is bullish on Brazil's economy after winning 75 new all-cargo charter allocations from the United States Department of Transportation (DOT), a company official told Reuters.
"We work with one freight forwarder and they are very, very upbeat about Brazil," Southern Air Senior Vice President Asa Hemperley said.

On December 31, the DOT awarded Southern Air Transport, of Columbus, Ohio, 75 flights, Florida West International Airlines of Miami, 25 flights, and Tower Air Inc of Jamaica, New York, 25 flights, leaving 175 flights in the charter pool, according to the award document. Southern Air and Florida West are privately held.
DOT also modified the the charter pool rules to allow new entrant carriers to apply for up to eight flights per month, according to the department document.

These 300 additional all-cargo charter flights are part of the 1996-1997 cargo charter proceedings. They were the result of an October 24 agreement by the two countries expanding the number of flights. Earlier 450 all-cargo charter flights had been awarded, according to the DOT document.
The 300 additional flights were in high demand. Nine carriers filed applications seeking a total of 678 charters, the DOT document said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
